correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, unique completion of any pair of first-two-coordinate placements to S3 yields six 2D chessboard blocks, pairwise n-point intersections along K3,3, and no triple intersections. Graph-of-spaces homotopy colimit gives the 9n-5 extra circles. At n=3 free-face collapses yield 4 circles; at n=4 local links, global parity orientation and Euler characteristic give a torus; for n>=5 the 1994 connectivity theorem makes each 2D block simply connected, and Hurewicz/Whitehead with exact f-vector yields the sphere wedge rank n^3-6n^2+8n-1. Standalone exact enumeration checks n=3..7 independently as samples, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual literature and published-research comparisons distinguish the first-person all-n three-way matching-complex wedge and fundamental-group theorem from the stronger-looking but inapplicable ordinary chessboard connectivity/direct-summand results and from different graph functors. No inspected result implies the six-block gluing formula. Unindexed exact-parameter literature remains a risk. A primary survey of higher-dimensional chessboards and hypergraph complexes (Wachs, Section 9) was checked for stronger general coverage and found not to imply this result.
residual_risks: Searches do not certify priority; an unindexed hypergraph matching-complex decomposition could imply the result despite no exact match.
The 1994 journal issue is the earliest verified public appearance of the foundational chessboard source located; an earlier preprint could exist.
The non-equivariant wedge theorem does not determine actions of all three coordinate-permutation groups.

value.rationale: The full three-dimensional 3x3xn nonattacking-rook complex is a canonical tripartite hypergraph matching complex. Its six-block split explains a stable nonzero free fundamental group rank 9n-5 across arbitrarily large n, although every constituent ordinary chessboard is simply connected for n>=5; the n=4 stage contains six genuine torus summands. Complete integral homotopy types for an infinite natural family are a substantive structural invariant, not a small numerical refinement.
